s1.why: Selected option a, reversing which map is larger-scale. At equal print size, the 1:24,000 map generally depicts more local detail.
250 degrees is 180 degrees opposite a 70-degree outward bearing.

Correctly identifies close contours as steep terrain, but omits that the contour interval is the fixed vertical elevation difference between successive contour lines, which the question also asks for.
Option b correctly identifies the usual upstream-pointing contour V in a stream valley.
At 1:24,000, 2.5 cm is 60,000 cm or 600 meters on the ground.

Though informally worded, the learner correctly describes sighting a visible landmark on the bearing, walking to it, and repeating. Interpret “lines up with the needle” in the context of a compass already set to the desired bearing; it does not claim that following magnetic north is always the route.
